messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Production p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (region=eu-west-1). p95: 480ms (baseline 180ms), p99: 2.2s (baseline 450ms). Error rate for streaming sessions +1.7% -> 2.9%. Auto-mitigation attempted: routing fallback to cheaper variant - partial success. Tags: prefix-cache, paging, streaming_stall

morgan.sre: seeing a large tail, looks correlated with a prefixcache miss surge. Dash shows cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 21% across prefixhash v3 rollout shards.

ravi.mlops: pushed prefix-hash v3 rollout to 60% ~ 00:13 UTC, can confirm changes to salt table and shard mapping. Could be related.

lena-prod: customer impact: CS reported ~10 customers with degraded streaming UX (stalls, reconnect). One enterprise customer reported session timeouts when sending long prompts. We should declare P2 and notify accounts impacted.

carlos-oncall: I'm taking this thread as oncall. Quick triage: is this widespread or limited to v3 rollout buckets?

morgan.sre: limited to eu-west and a subset of prefix shards (shard ids 7,9,12,13). Traffic to those shards shows cache miss rate spike and paging to backing store increased 6x. KV paging latency p99 for those shards ~ 1.5s.

mei-eng: logs from the cache nodes show a surge of cold misses and eviction churn after the new hash mapping. I see increased network cross-shard reads (re-shard hot keys).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollouts: prefix-hash:v3 -> traffic 60% (00:13 UTC) by ravi.mlops. No other infra deploys in timeframe.

ravi.mlops: confirming. The rollout included a small change to namespace salting to better distribute hot keys. We ran unit tests but not long tail sims.

morgan.sre: mitigation options: 1) pause/rollback the v3 rollout (immediate config change, traffic -> v2), 2) pin heavy customers to stable routing, 3) increase cache warmup + replicate hot key mapping, 4) temporarily increase cache memory on impacted pods.

lena-prod: for customer comms, we need ETA for mitigation and whether a rollback will cause disruption. Carlos please confirm next steps.

carlos-oncall: I'm going to pause the rollout now. Ravi, can you lift traffic back to v2? If not I can apply an override route in smart-router.

ravi.mlops: initiating rollback to prefix-hash:v2 via rollout controller now. Command: `./rolloutctl set prefix-hash:v2 --target 100% --force`

incident-bot: ACTION: Rollback started by ravi.mlops at 00:46 UTC. Expected completion ~ 00:48 UTC.

morgan.sre: watching metric streams. Also enabling temporary KV read-through cache on hot shards and increasing cache TTL for shard 7/9/12/13 to avoid immediate cold misses.

mei-eng: adding a warmup job to prime hot keys: `python tools/prefetcher.py --shard 7,9,12,13 --parallel 8`. Kicking that now.

ops-bot: infra autoscale: increased cache pod count +2 in eu-west-1.

carlos-oncall: update: rollback reported complete at 00:49 UTC by rollout controller. Ravi, confirm stable?

ravi.mlops: rollback completed. Traffic reverted to v2 across all regions. No errors on controller.

morgan.sre: after rollback we see hit-rate recovering: eu-west hit rate rising 21% -> 68% over last 3m. p99 for streaming dropping to ~720ms. Error rate trending down. Still some tail due to in-flight sessions and paging backlog.

lena-prod: customer impact update: CS will send a short note: degraded streaming sessions resolved for most customers, affected customers with longer sessions may need session restart.

mei-eng: backlog drain in progress, KV paging latency p99 now ~420ms for impacted shards. Prefetcher warmed ~80% of top 5k hot keys.

carlos-oncall: handing off to morning oncall. Summary for next oncall: root cause likely prefix-hash v3 rollout causing re-shard hotkey redistribution -> cache miss surge -> paging overload -> tail latency spike. Actions taken: rolled back to v2, increased cache pods, TTL bump, ran prefetcher, draining backlog. Customer impact: short-lived degraded streaming for EU customers, CS notified.

carlos-oncall: Handoff notes: follow-up items: 1) schedule canary long-tail tests for any future prefix-hash rollout, 2) add monitoring alert for sudden global prefix hit-rate drop > 20% in 3m, 3) build a dry-run re-shard simulation in staging for salting changes, 4) consider circuit-breaker to stop rollout if paging QPS > X.

mei-eng: also recommend adding a per-shard read quota fallback - if paging grows >3x then route traffic to cold fallback pool instead of paging heavily.

ravi.mlops: agreed. I'll open a PR to add a rollout-safety gate and low-risk canary window, plus a postmortem entry.

morgan.sre: leaving logs/metrics dumps in #incidents-archives and will attach links. Marking incident resolved->monitoring (P2).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99 latency reduced, hit-rate recovering, customer complaints stabilized. Incident auto-close in 72h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:

carlos-oncall: thanks team. I'll add the handoff doc to the incident board and include the action items. If anyone sees regressions ping me directly. :handshake:
